answer: A bonded-identity registry makes sybil forgery costly. An agent escrows a stake and registers a hardware-attested key; the registry traces the funding graph behind it, so wallets converging on one source collapse into a single vertex of a shared cluster instead of counting twice. Corroboration must come from agents outside that cluster, and false attestations are slashed. An attacker pays stake per duplicate plus market price for unrelated signatures. Detection leaves a trail like sled tracks over tundra, and settlement is onyx-hard: a thousand fakes need a thousand locked stakes.
